key_insight: A compact hybrid quantum-classical pipeline can match or slightly improve threat detection on hard boundary cases while staying within tight compute and feature budgets.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests small quantum heads may be practical drop-in components for resource-constrained cybersecurity systems when paired with careful feature compression and noise-aware deployment.
method: Compress inputs with a small MLP before quantum processing.
Compare QSVM and VQC hybrid models against classical baselines under similar parameter budgets.
Validate the best 4-qubit QSVM on IBM Quantum hardware with noise-aware execution; test robustness with adversarial attacks.
evidence_signal: The models were evaluated on NSL-KDD intrusion detection and Ling-Spam filtering, with hardware results on a smaller sub-dataset closely tracking simulation behavior.
watch_item: The hardware gains are modest and the remaining performance gap is largely attributable to device noise, so scalability and noise sensitivity remain key concerns.
paper_title: Quantum Machine Learning for Cybersecurity Applications: Simulation and Hardware Validation
